title: Day 75 · Week 10, Day 5 — Protocol: the hundred-and-fifty-minute plan — what the minutes do to diabetes, blood pressure and mood, the one woman in eight who gets there, the talk test, and a calendar built for two
summary: The Protocol episode for week 10 turns the 150-minute guideline into a week. What the dose buys: in randomized trials, exercise alone cut the odds of gestational diabetes, gestational hypertension and preeclampsia by about 40% each, with ~140 minutes of moderate activity a week needed for at least a 25% reduction (Davenport 2018, 106 studies, 273,182 women), and cut the odds of prenatal depression by two thirds in five trials, though not postpartum depression or anxiety. In overweight and obese women, aerobic exercise lowered preterm birth (RR 0.62; Magro-Malosso 2017). The dissent: an older Cochrane review (Han 2012, 5 trials) found no clear effect on gestational diabetes, dominated by a trial where only about half the exercise group exercised. Only ~13% of US pregnant women meet the guideline (Hesketh & Evenson 2016), and self-report overestimates moderate activity by about an hour a week. WHO 2020, ACOG 804 and the Canadian guideline agree on at least 150 minutes over at least three days with strength work, every minute counting. Intensity by talk test and Borg 12–14, strength rules, the sickness weeks, sitting, the postpartum continuation, the stop list, a template week for active and newly active women, and the couple rule: a shared calendar, three sessions together, both totals counted.
action: Tonight, open a shared calendar and put in next week's 150 minutes: five 30-minute blocks, two marked strength, at times she chooses around her sickness, at least three marked together. Add your own 150 minutes to the same calendar. On Sunday, write both weekly totals on the back page of the pregnancy file.
